name: Starship Flight 5
payload: None (test flight); Ship 30 itself, on a suborbital trajectory
delta_v: ~7.7 km/s (suborbital: speed at SECO, about -15 x 212 km)
first: First Super Heavy booster caught by the launch tower's arms
description: Starship's fifth flight test lifted off from Starbase, Texas, on 2024-10-13 at 12:25 UTC. Booster 12 separated at about 70 km, turned back with a boostback burn and flew to the launch tower, where it slowed to a near hover and was caught by the tower's arms 6 min 52 s after liftoff, the first booster caught that way. Ship 30 continued on a suborbital trajectory of about -15 x 212 km at 26.2° inclination (its low point below the surface, so it could not stay in orbit), re-entered over the Indian Ocean belly-first, flipped upright, fired its landing burn and splashed down near a pre-placed buoy 1 h 5 min 38 s after liftoff. It was not built to be recovered; a large fireball erupted about 16 seconds after it hit the water.

events.label: LAUNCH
events.note: Super Heavy B12 and Ship 30 lift off from Starbase 2024-10-13 12:25 UTC.

events.label: TOWER CATCH
events.note: Booster 12 is caught by the launch tower's arms 6 min 52 s after liftoff, after its landing burn.

events.label: SECO
events.note: Ship 30's engines cut off 8 min 25 s after liftoff, on a suborbital trajectory of about -15 x 212 km.

events.label: RE-ENTRY
events.note: Ship 30 enters the atmosphere belly-first over the Indian Ocean 48 min after liftoff.

events.label: SPLASHDOWN
events.note: Landing flip and burn, then splashdown near a buoy 1 h 5 min 38 s after liftoff; a large fireball erupts about 16 s later.
